name: What Data Cannot Tell You
title: What Data Cannot Tell You
answer: What Data Cannot Tell You is the idea that numbers from tests and attendance record only a slice of a student's learning and life. It matters because choices about students are better when data is joined with what teachers and other adults know from personal knowledge of the student. Treating measurable things as the whole picture can push aside educational goals that matter but are hard to count.

crumbs.name: Assessment, Data, and the Early Warning System

sections.body: Data systems capture only a portion of what happens in a student's education. A score cannot reveal qualities such as curiosity, kindness, creativity, or resilience, and an attendance record cannot explain the reason a student was absent. Teachers notice many things that no system stores. The problem this idea solves is the risk of making decisions from incomplete information, as when a score drop hides a family crisis or average scores hide strong growth from a difficult starting point. Seeing the whole student requires people as well as data.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: The text does not assign this idea to particular grade bands. In any classroom, teachers can pair formal data with their own observations and knowledge of students when discussing concerns or progress. School leaders can build routines where data reviews include time for adults to share context that numbers miss. Districts can set expectations that data informs decisions rather than replacing professional judgment. The aim is to keep the measurable information in service of the school's larger mission.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The supplied text gives no study, figure, or evidence label for this idea. It presents the point as a matter of practice and professional judgment rather than research. The examples it offers, such as a score dip linked to a family crisis or average scores reflecting growth from a hard start, are illustrations of why context matters, not findings from a study. On the text provided, this idea rests on practice rather than research.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The text warns districts against treating whatever can be measured as the only thing that counts. It notes that some of education's most important goals are difficult to measure. A data system that takes attention away from those goals can cause harm even if every number in it is correct. Data should support the mission and not become the definition of it. Decisions about students remain with people who know them, and the text places responsibility on adults to combine data with that knowledge.
